Fury Warrior Rotation in 

Fury Warriors revolve around maximizing Enrage uptime and dealing damage through fast-paced attacks and a variety of special abilities, excelling at dealing high multitarget damage while sacrificing little to no single target to do so.

Avoid Downtime - Fury generates the majority of its rage from abilities, so reducing the amount of time spent chasing, running out mechanics, or otherwise not hitting the boss is critical to maximizing performance. There are several abilities to help with this, such as Charge and Heroic Leap, so use them smartly to stay on target as much as possible!

Keep Abilities on cooldown - nearly every rotational Fury ability generates rage, though only Rampage spends it, and in large amounts. This makes it very important to ensure that abilities are constantly being used to ensure that Enrage is constantly maintained, even to the point of delaying Rampage in order to use rage more efficiently.

Avoid wasting Rage - unlike most resources, rage starts from zero and decays out of combat. Making efficient use of it, both in combat and by reducing the amount of time spent moving from one combat to another, will help maintain the rotation and eliminate downtime spent waiting for more resources. 

Reading Priority Lists
Abilities and talents are listed from highest to lowest priority in the Fury Warrior rotation. Every time an ability is cast, begin again at the top of the list and move down until there is something that can be cast, then return to the top once more.

Fury Warrior Starter Guide

 Best Fury Warrior Rotation

For all forms of content, Fury follows a priority list of what spells to cast. Below, we break down the main priority lists for Fury Warriors: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and various openers.

New in Patch 12.0.5: Rampage now triggers Reap the Storm when hitting 3+ targets, though it is already highly prioritized, so the rotation remains unchanged. Rend is also now applied automatically by Improved Whirlwind in multitarget situations, though it is still very slightly more optimal to use it directly against single targets.

 Best Fury Warrior Single Target Rotations

The single target rotation revolves around generating rage and using Rampage to convert it into Enrage. The bulk of the rotation is then filled by a combination of Bloodthirst, Execute, Raging Blow, and Whirlwind or Thunder Clap, creating two similar yet distinctive playstyles.

 Best Fury Warrior AoE Rotation

Improved Whirlwind allows Fury to cleave its normal single target rotation to 4 additional targets, fitting naturally into the rotation and allowing very easy access to cleave damage with little setup or single-target damage loss. This makes the multitarget rotation very similar to the single target one, with the added step of ensuring the Whirlwind buff is always active and saving cooldowns to align burst with the greatest number of targets.

 Best Fury Warrior Opener

Differing from many specializations, the Fury opener is virtually identical to its single-target priority, with the main goal of triggering Enrage as soon as possible. While pre-casting Recklessness was an important technique in the past, Odyn's Fury and new Apex talents make it no longer necessary.

Unless there are upcoming adds or an increased damage phase, stat increasing trinkets and combat potions are best used on the pull aligned with Recklessness/Avatar, heroism, and other cooldowns. In the case of longer fights with two potions, the second should be saved for a following set of adds, increased damage phase, or Execute whenever possible, though take care to use it early enough that combat won't end before those buffs do.

Execute timing varies, depending on Sudden Death procs.
Storm Bolt is an extremely minor damage increase when used during Bladestorm, though it is not worth talenting at the expense of survivability or mobility.

Because it deals damage in an area, Whirlwind can be cast mid-charge to trigger its buff before going into the full rotation.
If additional targets are coming up soon after the pull, cooldowns should always be saved for them instead of being used in the opener.

Odyn's Fury is used before opening cooldowns, in order to avoid further cluttering the already busy rotation.
Because the goal is to keep Bloodbath on cooldown and use Rampage in between as much as possible, Thunder Blast is only prioritized when it has two stacks available in order to prevent overcapping. Otherwise, Thunder Clap, Sudden Death, and Crushing Blow should be used as fillers in between those more important abilities.
Recklessness and Avatar are both affected by Anger Management, and so they may be macroed together for ease of use.

Because Thunder Blast has a high priority during Avatar, there is no need to preemptively apply the Whirlwind buff.
Recklessness and Avatar are both affected by Anger Management, and so they may be macroed together for ease of use.
If additional targets are coming up soon after the pull, cooldowns should always be saved for them instead of being used in the opener.

Pre-Combat Checks

Before any form of combat, whether raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content, ensure that Battle Shout is active on yourself and all relevant party members. In higher-end content, applying a food buff, flask, weapon oils, and preparing a combat potion is also a good idea.

 Fury Warrior Major Cooldowns

Increases rage generation to enable much more regular use of Rampage, further enhanced by the apex talent Rampaging Berserker. With its cooldown reduced by Anger Management and aligning perfectly with Avatar, it should have a fairly high uptime over the course of a dungeon or encounter.

A basic damage increase, this is a much more important cooldown for Mountain Thane, due to the influence of Storm Surge, Avatar of the Storm, and Capacitance. It should align perfectly with Recklessness and may therefore be macroed together, though Slayer will instead talent into Bladestorm.

A secondary cooldown used exclusively by Slayer, it deals a good amount of single and multitarget damage, while also triggering supplementary effects such as Violent Euphoria and Unhinged. It has a unique form of cooldown reduction, so it will not always align with other cooldowns, making it important to think about when to use the cooldown and when to save it.

A talented AoE attack and the focus of Midnight's first seasonal tier set. Dealing a good amount of single and multitarget damage, it also automatically triggers enrage, making it a good initiator.

A talented attack in the class tree, which serves more of a utility role in keeping enemies within an area, though its damage is rather mediocre. The ability can be reactivated to leap to the spear, though this has very niche applications.

 Fury Warrior Advanced Tips

Fury Warriors are very straightforward damage dealers, with a very flat damage profile not concentrated entirely into cooldown windows. Because of this, the biggest optimization is simply maximizing uptime on the target - knowing what mechanics are coming before they actually happen will help plan movement to minimize time spent off target, allowing more rage to be generated and more GCDs to be fit into the overall rotation.

There are a variety of tools to help with this, from using Heroic Leap to move out of range at the last moment before damage goes out, to using Charge after a target has finished moving, which are largely a byproduct of time and experience.

Fury Warriors have several cooldowns, but they're all used more or less the same way - on cooldown as much as possible. When situations or timers allow, cooldowns can be aligned, but they should not be delayed by a significant amount (typically no less than 10-15% of their actual cooldown) unless the delay will allow them to hit multiple targets when they would otherwise hit one, or it will be your final use of the cooldown before the end of the fight regardless.

The reason is that losing an entire use of a cooldown is typically a bigger loss than what is gained by stacking the cooldown with something else to amplify it. Some cooldowns, like Recklessness and Avatar will always align naturally, though others will not, so anticipating those timers and knowing when adds or important damage phases are coming is key.
